static_traits.name: Lin Kailing
static_traits.family_status: Has two sons, lives with husband
static_traits.social_status: Husband supportive, but self-rated contribution insufficient in camping-related interactions, relationship affected
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy or psychiatric visits; never had similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear speech, coherent thinking; rather negative, tense tone; able to cooperate and proactively describe troubles; Self-denial and comparison present

basic_info.main_problem: Often feeling incapable and useless in camping activities (especially pitching tents), this sense of insufficiency starting a year ago from a tent-pitching setback during a family camping trip, worsening when planning or doing camping, leading to Anxiety and stress, affecting enjoyment of family trips and self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing these feelings are affecting self-esteem and the overall enjoyment of family camping, hopes to improve self-esteem and the experience during family camping through counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not as good as others

special_situations.event: Failed to pitch the tent during a family camping trip a year ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot pitch the tent skillfully, it means I am very incompetent, and will ruin the family's experience
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Watching many instructional videos, asking experienced campers for advice, and afterward only participating in the simpler steps (such as fixing tent pegs)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined everyone's experience, I am a useless camper

special_situations.event: Every time planning or discussing future camping trips
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform worse than others, I will be looked down on, disappointing family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Because of embarrassment, reduces discussing this specific issue with her husband
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am going to mess things up again

special_situations.event: Completed smaller tasks at the campsite such as fixing ground pegs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only completing 'big tasks' counts as real contribution, small tasks do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or belittling one's own small progress, not acknowledging it
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not worth mentioning, I am still terrible

special_situations.event: Seeing others easily set up tents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not done as well as others, it equals incapability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with others to verify one's own insufficiency
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them / I am not capable

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen by family as capable and recognized, creating enjoyable camping experiences for the family
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing family, being seen as incapable and a failure
defense_goal: Avoids being judged by reducing talk about failure and self-deprecation, maintains a sense of safety and self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: An insufficient, incapable family member with inadequate contribution
object_relations.object_representation: Others/family who are capable and may judge oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When planning camping and family expects one to participate in tent setup
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding family's expectations as judgment and negation, thinking 'they will think I am no good'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Mainly Empathy and Clarification, gently pointing out 'this is your worry not fact', inviting evidence and counter-evidence; soft tone, slow pace, avoiding blame.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the husband proposes communicating or discussing camping skills, offering support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing discussion will expose one's own incapability, triggering embarrassment and shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First normalizing shame, use supportive statements and short sentences, inviting small-step expression of specific feelings and needs, avoiding excessive questioning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing others easily complete tent setup or division of labor
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking others' skillfulness as negation and belittling of oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopting Socratic Questioning, focusing on specific facts and observable evidence, helping distinguish facts from Interpretation; neutral tone, clear organization.

manifestations: Consciously 'useless / incapable' in camping activities, self-labeling as a 'useless camper'
Seeing small achievements as unimportant, difficulty experiencing value and meaning
Anxiety and stress when planning or participating in camping, questioning one's existential value (whether contributing to the family)
outcomes: Reduced enjoyment of and engagement in family trips

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeated self-criticism ('I am not good at anything')
Excessively worrying about 'messing up', hesitating and indecisive on site
Finds it hard to acknowledge small progress; lowers self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: When planning camping, presupposes 'they will think I am going to mess things up again'
Projecting feelings of self-incapability onto others' potential opinions, leading to avoiding communication and seeking help

exception_events.target_problem: When family camping requires pitching tents, the client usually feels incapable, Anxiety worsened, and thinks they will 'ruin everyone's experience', thus finding it hard to engage.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last camping trip, the client did not give up as usual, but proactively completed the task of securing tent pegs, contributing in that part.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different approach (watching tutorials beforehand, asking experienced people); different support (husband generally supportive); task splitting (focusing on the specific subtask of pegs), thus more bearable participation and small success emerged.

positive_force: Husband has a supportive attitude; can be an external resource
Willing to try small goals and gradual progress (willing to first practice the ground peg well)
Actively seeks tutorials and others' advice, showing learning motivation
Has completed a ground-peg task on site, with practical execution and learning ability
negative_force: Negating the positive and constantly comparing with others (lowering self-worth)
Significant anxiety and stress when planning or discussing camping
Reducing communication and help-seeking out of embarrassment, insufficient resource use
Overgeneralizing one failure into lasting incapability

target_behavior.behavior: Significant anxiety and Self-denial in camping-related situations ('I am very incompetent / will mess up')
antecedent: Arriving at the campsite and starting to set up the tent
Observing others complete tasks with ease
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralization and self-labeling after one setback, and comparison with others leading to decreased Self-efficacy and stronger shame
target_behavior.function: Avoids failure feelings and others' evaluation to protect self-esteem (self-defense)
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty engaging and enjoying camping, worsening Anxiety and stress, declining quality of family trip experiences

target_behavior.behavior: Due to embarrassment, reduces discussing camping difficulties and seeking help with the husband
antecedent: When husband or family talk about camping arrangements or skill improvement
When needing to prepare for upcoming camping
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and worry about being judged (mind reading others' negative evaluations)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being judged, avoiding exposing self-perceived incapability
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer chances to get support and guidance, the problem persisting and maintaining Anxiety around camping
